problem: Goal-oriented VLN (REVERIE, SOON) gives only terminal/distance feedback, so partial trajectories lack route-semantic supervision, and a single annotated path causes single-reference route bias although many routes can reach the same goal.
motivation: Goal-oriented instructions do not prescribe a route, so training signals for intermediate steps are weak. Route-following VLN data holds route-level knowledge that could be transferred to supply denser feedback and alternative demonstrations.
key_idea: Train a trajectory-to-language speaker on route-following VLN data, freeze it as a training-time evaluator, and use its reconstruction loss for progress rewards and for disagreement-aware reuse of trajectories.
insight: The abstract suggests that route knowledge transferred from a frozen speaker can serve as a training signal for goal-oriented navigators, with environmental success remaining the final criterion. Gains are modest and mixed: SR improves consistently, while SPL and OSR rise in some settings and fall in others. No ablation details are available from the abstract alone.
method: Cross-granularity route-prior transfer: a trajectory-to-language speaker is trained on route-following VLN data, then frozen as a training-time evaluator for goal-oriented tasks
Speaker Reconstruction Progress Reward: converts consecutive changes in the speaker's reconstruction loss along a trajectory into intermediate rewards
Disagreement-Aware Trajectory Reuse: interprets the speaker score together with the terminal outcome
Successful low-score paths are kept as alternative demonstrations; failed high-score paths are kept as hard replay cases
Inference: the navigator (DUET-based) keeps the original goal-oriented instruction and the speaker is absent

setting.backbone: DUET (trained with speaker-derived rewards and trajectory reuse); frozen trajectory-to-language speaker used only in training
setting.training_data: REVERIE / SOON goal-oriented data, plus route-following VLN data (e.g. R2R-style) for training the speaker; scales not given in the abstract
setting.privileged: none at test time (speaker is used only in training)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives only SR deltas (+1.42 REVERIE val-unseen, +1.32 SOON Unseen Houses, +2.22 SOON Unseen Instructions), not absolute values
results: On DUET, SMRKT improves SR by 1.42 points on REVERIE val-unseen, 1.32 on SOON Unseen Houses and 2.22 on SOON Unseen Instructions. SPL and OSR improve in some settings and drop in others.
limitations: Gains are small and SPL/OSR are inconsistent
Requires a separately trained speaker and route-following data, and evaluation is only on DUET with two datasets
